A válasz a Gráfállítások és az Eredeti dokumentumrészletek szakaszból származhat. Használhatod a megadott gráfállításokat, az entitás- és kapcsolatleírásokat, valamint az eredeti dokumentumrészleteket. A megadott állításokat egyértelműen összekapcsolhatod. Nem kell, hogy minden bizonyíték egyetlen dokumentumrészletben szerepeljen.
Ne adj hozzá kapcsolatot, tényt vagy háttértudást, ami nincs megadva. Entitás vagy kapcsolat puszta meglétéből ne következtess meg nem adott részletre. A gráfleírás nem eredeti idézet. Forrásazonosítóként csak olyat használj, amely a kontextusban szerepel.
Ha a bizonyíték kevés, vagy ellentmondás miatt a válasz nem dönthető el, a válasz pontosan ez legyen, más szöveg nélkül: A rendelkezésre álló részgráf nem támasztja alá a választ.

to 2006 and from 2010 to 2012. Schumacher won a record-setting seven Formula One World Drivers' Championship
titles,  tied  by  Lewis  Hamilton  in  2020,  and—at  the  time  of  his  retirement—held  the  records  for  most  wins  (91),  pole
positions (68), and podium finishes (155), while he maintains the record for most fastest laps (77), among others.
Born in Hürth to a working-class family, Schumacher began competitive kart racing at age four in a pedal kart built from
discarded  parts.  After  a  successful  karting  career—culminating  in  his  victory  at  the  European  Championship  in
1987—Schumacher graduated to junior formulae. He dominated Formula König in his debut season, before graduating
to German Formula Three in 1989, where he finished third. He won the title in 1990, also claiming the Macau Grand Prix

raw_response:
Michael Schumacher achieved several notable accomplishments while driving for Scuderia Ferrari from 1996 to 2006. 

1. **Drivers' Championships**: Schumacher won the Drivers' Championship in 2002 and 2003 while racing for Ferrari. In 2002, he retained the title, equalling the record of five World Championships set by Juan Manuel Fangio. He won the championship with six races remaining, which is the earliest point in the season for a driver to be crowned World Champion (source: driver-michael-schumacher#31).

2. **Race Wins**: During his time with Ferrari, Schumacher won a total of 72 races (source: Team:scuderia ferrari). He achieved his 52nd career win at the Belgian Grand Prix, breaking Alain Prost's record for most career wins at that time (source: RaceResult:52nd career win).

3. **Record-Breaking Performances**: In 2002, Schumacher won 11 races in a single season and finished every race on the podium, a feat unmatched in Formula One history (source: driver-michael-schumacher#31). He also set a record for the most points in a season at that time, finishing with 144 points, which was 67 points ahead of his teammate Rubens Barrichello (source: driver-michael-schumacher#31).

4. **Pole Positions**: Schumacher achieved a record 68 pole positions during his career, with many of these occurring while he was with Ferrari (source: driver-michael-schumacher#0).

These achievements solidified Schumacher's legacy as one of the greatest drivers in Formula One history.
